snippet.title: The Rosetta Mission and the History of the European Space Agency ESA (Documentary, 2014)
snippet.description:
For science, the breathtaking landing of the philae lander on Comet 67P is as sensational as the landing on the moon in 1964. The Rosetta mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) was designed to study the evolution of the Solar System by exploring one of the oldest heavenly bodies – comets. The mission unveiled secrets about our existence and the genesis of the solar system. The mission consisted of the Rosetta orbiter and the Philae lander. The probes were launched on 2 March 2004, travelled 6.4 billion kilometres in 10 years and, with the help of a few planet swing-bys, arrived at Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko on 6 August 2014. On 30 September 2016 the orbiter philae started its controlled descent.

snippet.title: They Turned Garbage into Gold (Literally, It Was A Lie)
snippet.description:
In the 90s, Waste Management was the king of trash. They claimed to be turning garbage into Wall Street gold, but in reality, they were just cooking the books. This is the story of how executives used "creative depreciation" (a fancy word for lying) to inflate profits by $1.7 billion while their trucks were rusting apart.

This documentary isn't just about trash; it's about the auditor, Arthur Andersen. Before they collapsed with Enron, they were busy helping Waste Management cover up one of the largest corporate frauds in history. We expose the "Action Steps" they used to hide the losses and how greed blinded everyone.

If you want to see another massive fraud enabled by bad auditors, watch our breakdown of the Luckin Coffee scandal: https://youtu.be/tWGFbqw7J4A

A masterclass in how to lie with numbers until you get caught.

snippet.title: The Manhunt for France's Most Notorious  Nazi collaborator
snippet.description:
For nearly 45 years, one of France's most notorious Nazi collaborators managed to evade justice.

Paul Touvier was not a German officer. He was a French citizen who rose through the ranks of the Milice, the feared paramilitary force that worked alongside Nazi occupiers during World War II. Accused of helping hunt resistance fighters and implicated in the execution of seven Jewish hostages in 1944, Touvier disappeared after the war and spent decades hiding under false identities.

His story is one of collaboration, betrayal, political controversy, and one of the longest manhunts in modern French history.

In this documentary, we uncover the life of Paul Touvier, his role during the Nazi occupation of France, the decades he spent as a fugitive, and the historic trial that made him the first French citizen convicted of crimes against humanity for actions committed during World War II.

From the dark days of Vichy France to the courtroom battles of the 1990s, this is the shocking true story of a man who spent half a century running from his past.

snippet.title: Life After Chernobyl and Fukushima | Full Documentary
snippet.description:
Thirty years after Chernobyl and five years after Fukushima, millions of people continue to live on lands quietly marked by radioactive contamination.

This documentary enters the “grey zones” of Belarus, Norway, and Japan, where the consequences of nuclear disaster are not only historical, but part of everyday life. After Chernobyl, the scientific program Ethos was launched with support from France and the European Union to work directly with communities in contaminated territories, helping residents identify daily risks, adapt their behaviors, and continue living in affected areas.

In central Norway, heavy fallout from Chernobyl deeply disrupted the lives of the Sami people, whose traditional reindeer herding practices were severely impacted by radioactivity. Decades later, Japan faced similar questions after Fukushima, where Ethos-inspired meetings brought together people from Belarus, Norway, and Japan to share experiences, fears, knowledge, and survival strategies.

Through rare personal testimony and unique encounters across three countries, the film asks urgent human questions: What does it mean to live in a contaminated territory? What risks remain invisible? And how do communities rebuild daily life in the long shadow of nuclear disaster?

localized.title: Life After Chernobyl and Fukushima | Full Documentary
localized.description:
Thirty years after Chernobyl and five years after Fukushima, millions of people continue to live on lands quietly marked by radioactive contamination.

This documentary enters the “grey zones” of Belarus, Norway, and Japan, where the consequences of nuclear disaster are not only historical, but part of everyday life. After Chernobyl, the scientific program Ethos was launched with support from France and the European Union to work directly with communities in contaminated territories, helping residents identify daily risks, adapt their behaviors, and continue living in affected areas.

In central Norway, heavy fallout from Chernobyl deeply disrupted the lives of the Sami people, whose traditional reindeer herding practices were severely impacted by radioactivity. Decades later, Japan faced similar questions after Fukushima, where Ethos-inspired meetings brought together people from Belarus, Norway, and Japan to share experiences, fears, knowledge, and survival strategies.

Through rare personal testimony and unique encounters across three countries, the film asks urgent human questions: What does it mean to live in a contaminated territory? What risks remain invisible? And how do communities rebuild daily life in the long shadow of nuclear disaster?

snippet.title: How a Teenage Boy Fooled the Nazis and Lived - The incredible story of film producer Gene Gutowski
snippet.description:
Film producer Gene Gutowski (Repulsion, Cul-de-Sac, The Pianist) was fourteen years old when first the Soviets then the Nazis invaded his hometown of Lwow, Poland. With a combination of chutzpah, cunning and an unflinching will to live, he survived the war flirting with danger as a teenage boy hiding in plain site. 

Witnessing first-hand the unspeakable horrors of the Nazi occupation, frequently cheating death and losing his entire family, Gutowski's journey is ultimately one of hope. As recounted with humour and pathos to his son, filmmaker Adam Bardach, his remarkable story represents a thumb of the nose at darkness and totalitarianism.

snippet.description:
One banker, one bad bet, and the whole world collapsed. It sounds like 2008, but this was 1772. This is the incredible story of Alexander Fordyce, the man whose reckless gambling in London triggered a domino effect that destroyed banks in Amsterdam, bankruptcies in Scotland, and credit freezes in the American colonies.

We explain how bills of exchange worked like primitive "crypto" and how this financial chaos helped trigger the American Revolution. History doesn't repeat, but it rhymes.

snippet.title: Evergreen vs Titanic The Ships That Sank Global Economies
snippet.description:
What do the Titanic and the Ever Given have in common? More than a century apart, both ships revealed a harsh truth about global trade: our modern economy is built on fragile systems. This video dives deep into how the Titanic’s tragic sinking and the Ever Given’s infamous blockage became metaphors for economic overconfidence, efficiency obsession, and systemic vulnerability.

Through a story-driven narrative, you’ll explore the hidden mechanics of global logistics, insurance markets, and financial interdependence. Each chapter breaks down how small disruptions—whether an iceberg or a gust of wind—can ripple across continents, freezing economies and exposing the brittle reality behind globalization.

By blending history, economics, and storytelling, this documentary-style video reveals the invisible forces shaping your daily life: from the supply chains behind your favorite products to the corporate incentives that keep the system running at full speed. In the end, it asks the ultimate question: can modern economies survive their own efficiency?

If you’re passionate about global economics, history, and how fragile modern prosperity truly is, this is the video you won’t want to miss.

snippet.title: How do snakes swallow animals so much bigger than they are? - Niko Zlotnik
snippet.description:
Explore how snakes evolved, and find out how their jaw-dropping anatomy allows them to take down prey several times their size.

--

Since slithering onto the scene some 150 million years ago, evolving length and limbless-ness out of their ancestral lizard forms, snakes have diversified rapidly. Their noodly bodies and flexible heads granted them access to novel places and prey. And today, there are nearly 4,000 snake species, spanning habitats high and low. Niko Zlotnik explores how snakes evolved into incredible predators.

snippet.title: How to Profit from a Recession: A Guide to Investing During an Economic Collapse.
snippet.description:
Ever wondered how to profit from a recession? This video is a guide to investing during an economic collapse. And here's a tip: the younger you are, the more you're going to want to pay attention.

More and more headlines are declaring a recession is due in 2020. But what even causes a recesssion? And if a recession was so bad, why would someone like Warren Buffet say he "hopes to see more recessions"? And more importantly: what can YOU do during a recession to come out on top?

******

📸 IG: james.v.j // https://bit.ly/2TOaBBC
🐦 Twitter: @jamesvjani // https://bit.ly/2zYPrsT



******

RULES OF A RECESSION.
A country is often described to be in a 'recession' when its GDP has been declining for 6 months in a row (although sometimes this definition varies depending on who you ask). 
With that being said, there are some important rules to keep in mind if you want to profit from a recession. The first rule being: nobody can time the market. No matter what, nobody knows WHEN is the next recession. 

But once a recession does hit, it’s important to not panic and start selling all your assets, because one thing is for sure: the market will always bounce back. But since the market is always shrinking and expanding, that also means that the market will always eventually crash. 

HOW TO PREPARE FOR A RECESSION…
Preparing for a recession is perhaps the most important part of this whole game. It’s very important that you start to save up money, build capital, avoid debt, and build a healthy credit score. You want to make sure that you have all the resources ready to make the most from that economic collapse. There’s nothing worse than seeing so many opportunities in-front of you, but no ways to take advantage of them.

WHAT HAPPENS DURING A MARKET CRASH?
When an economies market crashes (for whatever reason) one can expect an increase in unemployment levels, business bankruptcy, and three very important things to rise: death, divorce, defaults. 

HOW TO INVEST DURING A RECESSION?
When the market crashes, people become desperate to sell their assets like shares, and real estate. And the more motivated someone is to sell something, the likelier they are to sell it for cheaper. 

That’s where you come in. 

If you’ve prepared for the recession properly, then you should have a good amount of capital saved up and ready to invest back into the economy. Why invest back into the economy? Remember: the market will always bounce back. And everything is on a discount during a recession. That means you get to buy assets for way below market value, and then sell those very assets once the market bounces right back up – which it always will.

snippet.title: Obesity, diabetes and heart disease rates skyrocketing... is sugar to blame? (Full Documentary)
snippet.description:
How did the food industry get us to stop asking the question: is sugar toxic? It all starts with a secret PR campaign dating back to the 1970s. For forty years, Big Sugar deflected all threats to its multi-billion dollar empire, while sweetening the world’s food supply. As obesity, diabetes, and heart disease rates skyrocket, doctors are now treating the first generation of children suffering from fatty liver disease. The sugar industry is once again under siege. They dodged the bullet once. Will they do it again?

-------

▷ 03:37 - The global increase in daily sugar consumption

Today, industry is deploying its old tactics and pulling out the old adage “we just eat too damn much.”  This time consumers aren’t buying it. The critics have gotten smarter, bolder, and madder and science is catching up. 
  
Pediatric endocrinologist, Dr. Robert Lustig thinks we’ve all been ‘frucked’ by industry. He’s evangelical, blaming sugar for a waiting room filled with obese kids with fatty livers. His flock of five million online followers grows daily. In the court of public opinion, he’s part of a leading group of experts who are putting sugar on trial. 
  
But Japan’s not waiting for the verdict. For the first time in history, their children are burdened with 
lifestyle diseases that their parents never faced. To counter a health crisis that could sink their economy, Japan’s introduced a radical new law that takes aim at another 'bottom line': the girth of the nation's waistlines.  
 
Pulling back the curtain on the sugar-coated tactics of an industry once again under attack, Sugar 
Coated provides a chilling feeling of déjà vu. Today the industry is back sweetening the message. But this time, history comes knocking.  
 
When the doors closed at the Great Western Sugar Company in Colorado in 1976, someone forgot to sweep the floor. Gathering dust in the archives were 1500 pages of internal documents exposing how the sugar industry used tobacco-style tactics to dismiss troubling health claims against their products. Denver dentist turned postdoctoral scholar at the UCSF School of Medicine, Cristin Kearns, knew she’d stumbled on something big: the industry’s secret playbook. Her mentor, Stan Glantz, the superstar professor from San Francisco who brought down Big Tobacco warns, it’s going to get dirty. 
 
While industry and science duke it out, are we sitting on a dietary time bomb?

Ten years on from the 2016 Brexit referendum, the UK is about to appoint its seventh Prime Minister in a decade — so was Brexit worth it? In this video we break down the real economic impact of Brexit: how much it actually cost the UK economy, why the doom-laden Treasury forecasts and the Leave campaign's £350 million NHS bus were both wrong, and what the data really shows about GDP, trade, the City of London, and business investment. We dig into the goods-versus-services split, why the people who voted Leave were hit hardest while the metropolitan elites worked around it, the great post-Brexit immigration paradox and the "Boriswave," whether Britain is really "poorer than Mississippi," and why both Brexit and the new "Rejoin" campaign rely on the same magical thinking. Finally, we look at Brexit as a global turning point — the first crack in the post-Cold-War order — and ask why ten years of arguing about Europe distracted Britain from the domestic problems actually driving its economic stagnation. Take a tour of the vast, underground network of the Paris Catacombs, and find out how this 18th century cemetery came to be.

For centuries, Parisians had buried their dead in the Cemetery of the Innocents. By the 18th century, the grounds had become overcrowded — spewing foul odors across the city. Residents worried that it posed a public health threat, and petitioned the government for a solution. But where could they move millions of remains? Stephanie H. snippet.title: The $600 Billion Lie How They Faked Everything
snippet.description:
How do you make billions of dollars appear out of thin air? This documentary exposes the shocking true stories behind WorldCom, Wirecard, and Lehman Brothers—three corporate giants that built empires on lies, fake money, and hidden debts, nearly destroying the global financial system in the process.

We dive deep into the mechanics of the deception to understand how these companies fooled auditors, regulators, and investors for years.

👇 THE SCANDALS COVERED IN THIS VIDEO:

1. WORLDCOM ($11 Billion Fraud):
Led by Bernie Ebbers, WorldCom committed the largest accounting fraud in American history at the time. By capitalizing "line costs" as assets instead of expenses, they artificially inflated their profits by over $3.8 billion. This segment explores the internal audit that uncovered the truth and the subsequent collapse of a telecom giant.

2. WIRECARD (The Missing $2 Billion):
The darling of the German tech industry, Wirecard was processing payments for questionable industries while inventing profits. We analyze the role of CEO Markus Braun and the fugitive COO Jan Marsalek, revealing how they fabricated €1.9 billion in cash reserves in Asian trustee accounts that simply did not exist.

3. LEHMAN BROTHERS (Repo 105):
The trigger for the 2008 Financial Crisis. Lehman didn't just make bad bets; they hid them. We break down the "Repo 105" accounting gimmick, which allowed them to temporarily move $50 billion of liabilities off their balance sheet at the end of each quarter to look healthier than they were.

These weren't just accounting errors; they were calculated massive crimes that forced governments to rewrite the rules with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) and Dodd-Frank regulations.

In this video, you will uncover:
* The psychology behind white-collar crime.
* Why "Big Four" auditors often miss the red flags.
* How these historical frauds reshape how we invest today.

Transparency isn't just a corporate duty; it is essential for your own financial future.

localized.title: The dark origins of Disney fairy tales - Claudia Schwabe
localized.description:
Dig into the infamous tales of the Brothers Grimm, and explore how these gory stories evolved as they spread around the world.

--

An evil stepmother demands a maiden’s lungs and liver; a girl is ripped from a wolf’s stomach; and sisters mutilate their feet to squeeze into a gold slipper. During the early 1800s, brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm gathered these unflinchingly gory details from stories circulating around what’s now Germany. Claudia Schwabe explores how these now-infamous tales evolved as they spread worldwide.

Lesson by Claudia Schwabe, directed by Skirmanta Jakaitė.
